_meta.what_this_is: What the people building, buying and doubting microreactors say about the business case, in their own words. Every line is a verbatim quote checked against a stored copy of its source. Where a publisher blocks automated access the quote is marked as taken from search results rather than a page read.
_meta.why_it_exists: The rest of this site is figures. This page is the argument behind them. The buyer and the sellers disagree with the critics about almost everything except one point, which is that the first units are expensive and somebody other than a normal customer has to pay for them.
_meta.note_on_dates: The Cheeky Pint interview predates the August 2026 Janus award — DeWahl describes Janus as a competition still to be run. It is quoted here because it is the clearest public statement of how Antares sequences its markets, not as current news.

groups.name: The builders
groups.note: Company founders and executives on why the business works.

voices.speaker: Julia DeWahl
voices.quote: we are building in particular for critical infrastructure, largely for the military. although we do think that as costs come down, there will be an interesting commercial market too
voices.what_it_means: The company's own sequencing, stated plainly: defense first, commercial when the cost curve allows. Anyone building the commercial case is working on the second half of this sentence.

sources.label: Cheeky Pint — Julia DeWahl of Antares on building nuclear reactors for the US military (transcript)
sources.quote: there will be an interesting commercial market too

voices.speaker: Julia DeWahl
voices.quote: premium power is where you need to go with nuclear
voices.what_it_means: The strategy in five words. Microreactor power is not competing with grid average price; it is sold where the buyer already pays far more, or cannot get power at all.

sources.label: Cheeky Pint — Julia DeWahl of Antares on building nuclear reactors for the US military (transcript)
sources.quote: premium power is where you need to go with nuclear

voices.speaker: Julia DeWahl
voices.quote: They're actually willing to pay above market rates for that
voices.what_it_means: On hyperscalers wanting clean, firm, 24/7 power. A willingness-to-pay claim about the largest commercial buyer, made by a company that says data centers are not its target market.

sources.label: Cheeky Pint — Julia DeWahl of Antares on building nuclear reactors for the US military (transcript)
sources.quote: They're actually willing to pay above market rates for that

voices.speaker: Julia DeWahl
voices.quote: So I would say it fast follows
voices.what_it_means: On oil and gas as a commercial market after defense. The commercial case is not a someday item in the company's own telling — it is the next one.

sources.label: Cheeky Pint — Julia DeWahl of Antares on building nuclear reactors for the US military (transcript)
sources.quote: So I would say it fast follows

voices.speaker: Jordan Bramble
voices.quote: we won the race to criticality, and now we've shifted to the race to commercialization
voices.what_it_means: Said on the $470M Series C in August 2026, after the Mark-0 reached criticality at Idaho National Laboratory on 4 June 2026. The company frames commercialization as the current problem, not the next one.

sources.label: The Defense Post — Antares to Fast-Track US Military Base Nuclear Microreactors With $470M Injection
sources.quote: we won the race to criticality, and now we've shifted to the race to commercialization

voices.speaker: Jordan Bramble
voices.quote: Energy scarcity is constraining America's most critical defense systems. Through Janus, Antares will deliver clean, firm, resilient power for the warfighter.
voices.what_it_means: The Janus pitch in one sentence: the constraint being sold against is scarcity at the point of use, not price.

sources.label: POWER — The Janus Five: 20+ Commercial Nuclear Microreactors, Starting in 2028
sources.quote: Energy scarcity is constraining America's most critical defense systems

voices.speaker: Tori Shivanandan
voices.quote: The U.S. Army is a savvy customer. They have the world's top nuclear experts and know what to look for in a partner. The numbers tell the story.
voices.what_it_means: On Radiant's $750M award, the largest of the five. The claim is that the government buyer is a competent technical judge — which is the argument for treating a defense award as a commercial signal.

sources.label: Radiant — Radiant Wins $750M Contract from U.S. Army
sources.quote: The U.S. Army is a savvy customer

groups.name: The buyer
groups.note: The U.S. Army and the Defense Innovation Unit on how Janus is structured and what it is for. These are the most consequential quotes on this page: they describe the contract that is actually being signed.

voices.speaker: Andrew Waksman
voices.quote: We want these to be commercial companies raising commercial dollars to produce commercial products. We're simply recognizing that no one is going to be able to sell their first reactor or the second reactor and be able to afford it on private dollars alone, so these milestone payments can be seen as a form of subsidy to help these companies get there.
voices.what_it_means: The government's own stated purpose for a $2.2bn program is to manufacture a commercial industry. It is the strongest public statement that the defense market is a bridge, not a destination.

sources.label: POWER — U.S. Army Mobilizes $2.2B Janus Program to Deploy More Than 20 Commercial Microreactors
sources.quote: We want these to be commercial companies raising commercial dollars to produce commercial products

voices.speaker: Andrew Waksman
voices.quote: it would transition to an Army power purchase agreement
voices.what_it_means: After the Defense Innovation Unit pays for construction and the first year of operation. A power purchase agreement is a commercial instrument; the Janus sites become PPA sites once the milestones are done.

sources.label: POWER — U.S. Army Mobilizes $2.2B Janus Program to Deploy More Than 20 Commercial Microreactors
sources.quote: it would transition to an Army power purchase agreement

voices.speaker: Andrew Waksman
voices.quote: One thing you definitely cannot do is divide the dollars by the number of reactors and have that be a relevant number.
voices.what_it_means: A direct warning against the obvious arithmetic. Radiant's $750M over 15 units is not $50M a unit: the award pays for development and the first units, which are the expensive ones.

sources.label: POWER — U.S. Army Mobilizes $2.2B Janus Program to Deploy More Than 20 Commercial Microreactors
sources.quote: One thing you definitely cannot do is divide the dollars by the number of reactors

voices.speaker: Andrew Waksman
voices.quote: These are Army licensed; they are not NRC licensed
voices.what_it_means: Janus reactors are authorized by the Army Reactor Regulatory Office, not the Nuclear Regulatory Commission. That is the single biggest structural difference between Janus and any commercial deployment, and the biggest reason a defense order book does not automatically convert into a commercial one.

sources.label: POWER — U.S. Army Mobilizes $2.2B Janus Program to Deploy More Than 20 Commercial Microreactors
sources.quote: These are Army licensed; they are not NRC licensed

voices.speaker: Andrew Waksman
voices.quote: we are expecting that the majority of the money is to be private
voices.what_it_means: The $2.2bn ceiling is not the project cost. Most of the capital is expected to come from the companies, which is why the Series C rounds and the award announcements arrive together.

sources.label: POWER — U.S. Army Mobilizes $2.2B Janus Program to Deploy More Than 20 Commercial Microreactors
sources.quote: we are expecting that the majority of the money is to be private

voices.speaker: Andrew Waksman
voices.quote: that was a deliberate decision based on the learning from NASA COTS
voices.what_it_means: On paying against hardware milestones rather than design reviews. The program is explicitly modeled on the contract that produced SpaceX — government as anchor customer, vendor keeps the asset.

sources.label: POWER — U.S. Army Mobilizes $2.2B Janus Program to Deploy More Than 20 Commercial Microreactors
sources.quote: that was a deliberate decision based on the learning from NASA COTS

voices.speaker: Andrew Waksman
voices.quote: These reactors are not going to provide 100% of the power on any of these installations, but they will be tied into the grid.
voices.what_it_means: The product being bought is resilience alongside the grid, not islanded supply. That matters for the commercial analogue: the buyer is purchasing firmness, not replacing a utility.

sources.quote: These reactors are not going to provide 100% of the power on any of these installations

groups.name: The skeptics
groups.note: The case against, from analysts and utility executives. It is here because the strongest objection — that shrinking a reactor raises its cost per watt — is confirmed by the national laboratory's own cost model, not contradicted by it.

voices.speaker: John Ketchum
voices.what_it_means: The sharpest one-line objection, from the head of the largest U.S. renewables developer. Small does not mean cheap; it can just mean a smaller unit of loss.

sources.label: Heatmap News — Data Centers Are Fueling a Tiny Nuclear Hype Cycle

voices.speaker: Bill Tilles
voices.what_it_means: Shrinking a reactor raises cost per watt rather than lowering it. Idaho National Laboratory's own model agrees: halving output raises levelized cost by about half, and its 7 MWt reference design prices at $980/MWh against $330 for the 20 MWt one. The open question is whether factory learning outruns it.

sources.label: Heatmap News — Data Centers Are Fueling a Tiny Nuclear Hype Cycle

voices.speaker: Dennis Wamsted
voices.org: Institute for Energy Economics and Financial Analysis
voices.quote: I think it's just as overhyped as it was a few years ago
voices.what_it_means: The counterweight to every order-book announcement on this site. Wamsted's position is that nothing in the last two years has changed the underlying economics.
